# Volume 1 — CHAPTER XXIV. Miss Thorne and Her Pupils Get Up a Concert

!!! note "Source text"
    Passages cited on the wiki pages link into this page. Only volumes at or before
    this page's cutoff are present.

OCTOBER had arrived once more by the time Nell was prepared to return to school—a magnificent October, entirely crimson and gold, featuring mild mornings in which the valleys were packed with subtle mists as though the autumn spirit had filled them up for the sun to drink dry—amethyst, pearl, silver, rose, and smoke-blue. Heavy dews caused the fields to shine like silver cloth, and large piles of rustling leaves rested in the hollows of many-stemmed woods, inviting one to run briskly through them. A yellow canopy hung over the Aspen Path, where the ferns were withered and brown along its entire length. A sharpness existed in the air itself, invigorating the spirits of young girls walking, contrary to snails, rapidly and eagerly toward school; and returning to the small brown desk next to Isolde brought great joy, while Opal Pettigrew nodded from across the aisle, Carrie Mott dispatched notes, and Julia Bell handed down a “chew” of gum from the rear seat. Nell inhaled a deep, happy breath while she sharpened her pencil and placed her picture cards inside her desk. Life was undoubtedly quite fascinating.
{: #nw-v01-c24-p0000 }

The newly arrived instructor proved to be yet another loyal and supportive ally for her. Miss Thorne, an intelligent and compassionate young lady, possessed the delightful talent for capturing and keeping her students' love while drawing forth their finest intellectual and moral qualities. Beneath this beneficial guidance, Nell blossomed like a blossom, returning to her household to give enthusiastic descriptions of her academic endeavors and ambitions to an appreciative Obed and a discerning Thirza.
{: #nw-v01-c24-p0001 }

“Thirza, my entire heart belongs to Miss Thorne. Her manners are so refined, and her spoken tone is exceedingly gentle. Whenever my name leaves her lips, I sense without a doubt that an E is included in the spelling. Recitations took place this afternoon. How I long for you to have been present while I delivered ‘Mary, Queen of Scots.’ My entire soul was poured into that performance. On the journey back, Opal Pettigrew mentioned that when I uttered the line, ‘Now for my father’s arm,’ and she noted, ‘my woman’s heart farewell,’ it chilled her blood completely.”
{: #nw-v01-c24-p0002 }

“Well now, one of these days, you could repeat it to me when we are out in the barn,” Obed proposed.
{: #nw-v01-c24-p0003 }

“Naturally I am going to,” Nell said thoughtfully, “though I am aware that I cannot perform it quite as effectively. The experience will lack the thrill of addressing an entire schoolroom of people who are listening intently to every sentence. I am certain that I cannot chill you to the bone.”
{: #nw-v01-c24-p0004 }

“Seeing those young boys go all the way to the summits of the large trees on Bell’s hill searching for crows’ nests this past Friday chilled her blood, according to Mrs. Sowerby,” Thirza remarked. “It surprises me that Miss Thorne promotes such behavior.”
{: #nw-v01-c24-p0005 }

“However, a crow’s nest was what we desired for studying nature,” Nell clarified. “It happened during our field afternoon. Thirza, field afternoons are marvelous. Furthermore, Miss Thorne provides such wonderful explanations for everything. Writing essays about our field afternoons is required of us, and my essays are the finest.”
{: #nw-v01-c24-p0006 }

“Claiming that yourself shows a great deal of vanity. Leaving such a remark for your instructor to make would be preferable.”
{: #nw-v01-c24-p0007 }

“Yet those were her exact words, Thirza. And truly it does not make me conceited. What reason have I to be, seeing that I am so terrible at geometry? Even so, I am actually starting to understand it just a bit now. Miss Thorne explains it with such clarity. Even so, I shall never excel at it, which I can promise you is a sobering thought. On the other hand, composing essays brings me great joy. Usually, Miss Thorne allows us to select our own topics; however, our assignment for next week is to compose an essay about a notable individual. Selecting just one from the vast number of notable individuals throughout history is difficult. Wouldn't it be wonderful to be notable yourself and have people compose essays about you once you have died? Oh, I would truly delight in being notable. I believe that upon becoming an adult, I shall train as a nurse and join the Red Crosses on battlefields acting as a messenger of mercy. That will be my path, provided I do not travel overseas as a foreign missionary. Becoming a missionary sounds exceedingly romantic, though it requires a person to be exceptionally righteous, which would prove to be an obstacle. Furthermore, we perform physical culture exercises on a daily basis. They impart gracefulness and aid your digestion.”
{: #nw-v01-c24-p0008 }

“Promote fiddlesticks!” declared Thirza, as she genuinely believed the entire matter was absurd.
{: #nw-v01-c24-p0009 }

Yet every physical culture contortion, recitation Friday, and field afternoon seemed insignificant compared to an initiative that Miss Thorne proposed during November. Her idea was for the students of Brierley school to organize a performance and present it inside the hall upon Christmas Night, aiming for the worthy objective of assisting in funding a flag for the schoolhouse. With the students without exception agreeing warmly to this proposal, work on a program commenced immediately. Furthermore, out of every thrilled future participant, not one felt as thrilled as Nell Harcourt, who devoted herself completely to the project, despite being hindered by the opposition of Thirza. To Thirza, the entire affair was sheer absurdity.
{: #nw-v01-c24-p0010 }

“Your minds are simply being crammed with foolishness, consuming hours that should be spent on your studies,” she complained. “Children organizing performances and hurrying off to rehearsals does not have my sanction. It renders them boastful, impudent, and eager for useless roaming.”
{: #nw-v01-c24-p0011 }

“However, consider the noble purpose,” begged Nell. “A flag will foster a patriotic feeling, Thirza.”
{: #nw-v01-c24-p0012 }

“Nonsense! The minds of every single one of you hold hardly any devotion to our country. Having a fun time is your sole desire.”
{: #nw-v01-c24-p0013 }

“Well, if you are able to mix patriotism and fun together, isn’t it fine? Naturally, organizing a concert is really wonderful. Six choruses are on our program, and Isolde will perform a solo song. I have parts in two dialogues—‘The Society for the Suppression of Gossip’ along with ‘The Fairy Queen.’ A dialogue will also be performed by the boys. On top of that, Thirza, I am scheduled for two recitations. Thinking about it makes me literally tremble, though it is a pleasant, exciting sort of tremble. To conclude the event, there will be a tableau—‘Grace, Hope and Charity.’ The performers in it will be Isolde, Opal, and myself, dressed in white drapery with our hair loose. Dressed as Hope, I must clasp my hands—like this—and look upward. My recitation practice will take place in the garret. If you listen to me groaning, do not feel frightened. A heartrending groan is required in one piece, and producing a proper artistic groan is actually difficult, Thirza. Flossie Tulk has become moody since she missed getting her desired role in the dialogue. Her wish was to play the fairy queen. Such a choice would be absurd, as a fairy queen with Flossie’s weight is unheard of. A fairy queen needs to be slim. The queen's part went to Odette Pullen, while I will act as a maid of honor to her. According to Flossie, a fairy with red hair is every bit as absurd as a heavy one, yet I refuse to let Flossie’s remarks bother me. My hair will feature a crown of white roses, and because I lack my own pair, Opal Pettigrew plans to loan me her slippers. After all, slippers are essential for fairies. Can you picture a fairy dressed in boots? Particularly ones featuring copper toes? The hall will be adorned by us using creeping spruce as well as fir mottoes filled with pink tissue-paper roses. Following the seating of the audience, everyone will process inside two by two to an organ march performed by Emma White. Oh, Thirza, though I realize your enthusiasm does not match mine, aren't you hoping that your little Nell brings honor to herself?”
{: #nw-v01-c24-p0014 }

“My sole wish is for you to act properly. When this whole commotion ends and you can finally quiet down, I will be truly relieved. With your mind completely consumed by tableaus, groans, and dialogues, you are currently entirely useless. Regarding your tongue, the fact that it isn't completely worn through is a wonder.”
{: #nw-v01-c24-p0015 }

Nell let out a sigh and went to the back yard, where the boughs of the leafless poplars framed a young new moon shining out of a western sky of apple-green, and where Obed was chopping wood. Sitting down on a block, Nell discussed the concert with him, certain that she had found a listener who was both appreciative and sympathetic, on this occasion if no other.
{: #nw-v01-c24-p0016 }

“Well now, I reckon it’s going to be a pretty good concert. And I expect you’ll do your part fine,” he said, looking down with a smile at her eager, lively little face. Nell returned his smile. Their friendship was exceptionally strong, and Obed frequently felt grateful that her upbringing was not his responsibility. Thirza handled that task entirely on her own; had it fallen to him, he would have been troubled by constant clashes between his desires and that obligation. Because of this setup, he had complete liberty to “spoil Nell”—to use Thirza’s expression—to his heart's content. Yet the situation worked out well enough; an occasional bit of “appreciation” can be just as beneficial as an abundance of dutiful “bringing up.”
{: #nw-v01-c24-p0017 }
